subject: Nanotechnology
title: Thermodynamics of Self-Assembly
description: A quick, practical guide to Thermodynamics of Self-Assembly.

hook.text: Self-assembly seems magical — but it obeys thermodynamics. Structures form because they lower the system's free energy.

buildup.text: Enthalpy favors bonding — attractive interactions release energy when components connect in the right arrangement.

discovery.text: Entropy can also drive assembly — releasing ordered water molecules from hydrophobic surfaces increases total disorder.

twist.text: The structure must sit at a free energy minimum — but kinetic traps can freeze assembly in wrong configurations.

climax.text: Reversibility is key — weak bonds let mistakes correct themselves, guiding assembly toward the intended structure.

punchline.text: Self-assembly works because mistakes can undo — weak bonds are the secret.

quiz.question: Why is reversibility important in self-assembly?
options: It prevents any structures from forming
Weak reversible bonds let misassembled components detach and reattach correctly, avoiding kinetic traps
Strong irreversible bonds always produce the best structures
